note: tools/run_job.py data/jobs/nominal_C.json --sim --scenario realistic --seed N --compare (camera loop vs dead reckoning, strict grasp) and --no-camera --lenient-grasp (dead reckoning to the end), seeds 1-3, plus --scenario slip --seed 1 (camera loop); the rows collected with run_job.sim_once (2026-10-06, the C: legs A 10, B 7, C 5 stones, 94 stones, wall distance 840 mm, stacked pick-up station). The true ARES path is checked against the legs, plates and the station table (mauer.simworld floor check).
discussion: - Camera loop, realistic: 94/94 seated in every seed (12/12 half stones), horizontal error max 3.88-4.01 mm, dominated by the errors outside the loop (1 mm UR-mount error and 1 mm holder scatter on the deck magazine, WorldErrors.realistic): the `slip` scenario gives 94/94 within 0.83 mm (seed 1). 6 station trips, 61-73 ARES moves per run.

- True ARES path (camera loop): no move touches a leg, plate or the table in the 4 runs; smallest gap to an obstacle 70-89 mm realistic, 60 mm slip. At the wall distance 840 mm the plates end 110 mm before the ARES front at a stop (740 mm: 10 mm - with the old 19-trip station a slip on the last closed-loop approach put ARES onto a plate in all 3 realistic seeds of the L, the C study at 740 mm once in 10 runs) - the open plate-gap decision of 2026-10-05 is settled by the larger distance.
- Seed 3: no start-pose overlap any more (at 740 mm the operator's start placement lay 16 mm on plates W1 / W2).

- Dead reckoning stops at a station pick (the gripper misses stone s00l2: seeds 1 and 3 on the first trip, seed 2 on the second, 15, 30, 15 stones placed); with a lenient gripper the 94 stones miss the pins by up to 172 mm (11, 15, 0 seated), 79, 78, 70 of the stones moved station -> magazine land off their holders (up to 241 mm) and ARES drives up to 59 mm onto the plates (plate W0, plate W6) - the reference case without the camera.
